newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Power NZ to take Waipa council, Mercury to court.
newsitem.headline: Power NZ to take Waipa council, Mercury to court.

text.p: Power New Zealand on Thursday said it would commence legal proceedings immediately against both the Waipa District Council and Mercury Energy Ltd over the council's decision to sell its shareholding in Power NZ to Mercury.
This morning the Waipa District Council accepted Mercury's $10/share offer for its 146,880 Power NZ shares.
The chairman of Power NZ's independent directors, Barry Brill, said in a statement that the Waipa District Council's decision was "unethical, immoral and illegal".
He said the council, with the encouragement of Mercury, had decided to break a legal contract which had seen it given 146,880 free shares in Power Nz.
These shares were given free to the council on the clear understanding that they could not sell them for a five year period, and the n only to a buyer approved by Power New Zealand," Brill said.

"This contract which was freely entered into by the council, remains in place. We will be vigorously asking the court that it be upheld and will also be seeking recompense for Mercury's actions in inducing the council to break its contract with us."
Utilicorp NZ, which is 79 percent owned by Utilicorp United Inc, is involved in a takeover battle with Auckland-based Mercury Energy for Power NZ.
Late this afternoon, UtiliCorp NZ said it would, on or after October 1, raise its offer for local authorities' shares in Power NZ to $7.25-$10 per share.
